name: mushroom curry sauce
instructions:
Basically a punjabi [[tikka-masala]] sauce — SAME SPICE STACK (cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, cardamom, kashmiri chili powder, amchur powder) — with three changes:

1. SHALLOT instead of onion.
2. MUSHROOMS added — ideally NOT cremini/portabella: the funky ones (TRUMPET, OYSTER, CHANTERELLE) are best (see notes).
3. NOT PUREED at the end — the shallots and diced tomatoes are small enough as is.

CREAM / BUTTER stays, as in the tikka sauce.

=== BUILD ===

Sauté the shallots, garlic, and mushrooms (vegetable oil + ghee, as in the tikka base), add diced tomatoes + tomato paste + the ground spice stack, simmer until reduced — then DO NOT BLEND. Finish with cream and butter.
notes:
=== WHY THIS OVER STANDARD TIKKA MASALA SAUCE ===

You get to EAT THE MUSHROOM, and you don't have to puree anything — the shallots and diced tomatoes are small enough. Same flavor register, less equipment, more texture.

=== THE MUSHROOMS — FUNKY ONES, NOT CREMINI/PORTABELLA ===

It's ideal to use NON-cremini/portabella mushrooms: the funky ones — TRUMPET, OYSTER, CHANTERELLE — are best. Their funkiness goes well with indian spices. Cremini/portabella are the workable-but-not-ideal fallback (secondary).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[tikka-masala]]: the parent — same punjabi masala spice stack, onion base, blended smooth, with the marinated-and-broiled protein component. This sauce is the chunky, no-blend, mushroom-forward fork of it.
why_i_like_this_recipe: I like it over standard tikka masala sauce because you get to eat the mushroom and you don't have to puree anything (the shallots and diced tomatoes are small enough).
